subject: tu:game/world/btricol
value: A reconstruction that addresses the right ADDRESS through the WRONG SYMBOL is invisible to every score-based screen in this project, and regnorm.py is the only tool that reports it. Measured on src/game/world/btricol.c. The TU declared `extern f32 gColQueryLine[8];` for the collision query line - a name that appears in NO other source file, is absent from config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt, and is DEFINED NOWHERE in the tree, while the target object relocates the same two words against lbl_8023F7E8 (.bss:0x8023F7E8) and the sibling TUs worldcol.c and gauntworld.c already spell that real name for the same memory. THE SCREENS THAT MISSED IT: fndiff --count scored the function real 30 both before and after the fix, because it normalises `lbl_*`-versus-name relocation differences as pool-name noise, so the two wrong-symbol words landed in the non-real remainder; objdiff fuzzy was 99.77 and unchanged; the masked byte scan behind webfrank_audit cannot see it at all, because an ADDR16_HA/LO field is filled by the linker and the instruction WORDS are identical; and the function's own live attempt record had therefore labelled the whole residual REGISTER_ONLY. THE SCREEN THAT CAUGHT IT: regnorm.py printed exactly two STRUCTURAL lines, `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA lbl` versus `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA gColQueryLine` with the annotation `[reloc target differs]`, and its verdict line refused the REGISTER_ONLY label at STRUCTURAL-PRESENT. This is the concrete case the tool's own header warns about, and it is why the mandatory rule is to run regnorm BEFORE trusting any inherited REGISTER_ONLY classification, including one written by a careful prior worker with full forensics. CONSEQUENCES OF THE FIX, all measured: the two STRUCTURAL words went to zero; TriLineCol moved from OPERAND_DIFF to regnorm-EXACT (0 renaming, 0 STRUCTURAL) and from 24 to 20 diff lines; BTriLineCol moved from OPERAND_DIFF to an honest REGISTER_ONLY; and `real` did not move on either function, which is precisely why the defect had survived. NOTE THE GATE INTERACTION: because the raw relocation bytes change while every score reads neutral, defake_gate.py check reports this correct fix as a REGRESSION ('raw bytes/relocs changed although every score reads neutral'). That flag is doing its job and must be arbitrated, not obeyed - read the two relocation lines with an aligned `fnasm --diff` and confirm they change from differing to `=` against the target, then rebaseline. RELATION TO THE FLIP LAW: this is claim.law.symbolified-own-pool-literal-blocks-tu-flip.20260831.v1 in its second form. There the invented extern pointed into the TU's OWN .sdata2 pool; here it pointed at a foreign .bss object. Both are latent `undefined: <symbol>` link failures that only surface at the flip attempt, and the general screen generalises accordingly: grep a near-flip TU for every `extern` whose name is neither in symbols.txt nor defined in the tree, not merely for `lbl_<ADDR>` names inside its own pool range. STILL OPEN FOR THIS TU: btricol.c owns .sdata2 0x80345D40-0x80345D70 per config/GUNE5D/splits.txt yet still declares `extern const f64 lbl_80345D40;` and `extern const f32 lbl_80345D50;` into that very range, so the flip law's original form remains unfixed here and btricol is NOT flip-ready. Their values are both zero (poolval.py --sweep), but substituting the literals is NOT free: spelling `zero = 0.0f` regressed BTriLineCol real 30 -> 157 by letting MWCC collapse an fmr the target emits, and the four pool entries at 0x80345D48/58/60/68 that TriLineCol's literals occupy are unreferenced by the current source, so the pool would also have to be reconstructed in order. Treat the btricol flip as its own claimed pass, not a tail-end step of a matching session.
